name: Solène Kiptanui-Dzhaksybekov
role: Gene-mod body artist and living canvas
location: Hamtramck Enclave, studio-squat above the Tallow Market
description:
Solène is a short, densely built woman whose body is her portfolio and her manifesto. Her skin shifts through a slow chromatic cycle — deep amber at rest, bleeding into violet around her joints when her temperature rises — the result of bioluminescent dermal graft work she has performed largely on herself over seven years. Her scalp is shaved on the left and grows a thick coil of natural hair on the right, threaded with fiber-optic strands that pulse in sync with her heartbeat. Her face is calm to the point of unnerving, large dark eyes framed by subdermal ridge implants that give her brow a faintly architectural quality. She smells faintly of the enzyme baths she uses to prep her graft medium.

Solène works at the edge of what the body can absorb and still call itself art. Her clients come to her not for decorative mods but for transformations — she specializes in grief work, helping people externalize trauma through bespoke biological alteration: scars that bloom into patterned keloid gardens, tear ducts rerouted to produce indigo pigment, fingernails replaced with translucent keratin windows through which capillaries are visible. She is meticulous, almost devotional in her craft, and utterly uninterested in anyone who cannot articulate exactly what they want to leave behind.

core_fears: Her work becoming fashionable and therefore hollow
Losing fine motor control before she has finished her own body
core_desires: To make the invisible legible on skin
To find one person who can witness her own transformation without flinching
blind_spots: Assumes everyone processes pain the same way she does — through externalization
Does not recognize when clients are self-harming under the guise of art
psychology.secret: The signature chromatic shift in her skin was not intentional — an early graft batch was contaminated and she nearly died; she has built her entire reputation on an accident she is too proud to admit.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise biological terminology mixed with quietly poetic phrasing; rarely uses slang; speaks in complete sentences
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, measured, with long pauses before answering — she thinks before she commits
verbal_tics: 'What does it need to say?' (when discussing a client's request)
'That's not what I asked' (when deflecting small talk)
example_lines: 'The body already knows what it's carrying. I just help it find the surface.'
'I don't do decorative. If you want decorative, there are seventeen studios in the Loft who will take your Quanta.'

story_hooks: A client comes in with a request that matches the biological signature of a Helix Biosystems proprietary graft — something that shouldn't be on a civilian's body
Solène's enzyme cultures begin dying in sequence — sabotage, contamination, or an E.L.F. she offended with a data offering she never made
narrative_function: Quest giver for body-modification subplots; information source on the underground biomod scene; can identify unusual augmentations or biological alterations on sight; provides local color representing the intersection of grief, identity, and physical transformation.
augmentations: Full-body bioluminescent dermal grafts (self-administered); subdermal brow ridge implants; fiber-optic hair threads; rerouted tear ducts producing blue-black pigment; no cyberware beyond a basic mesh-link for studio bookings
daily_life: Rises before dawn to check the enzyme cultures she keeps alive in a climate-controlled cabinet, then spends the morning doing precision graft prep work; afternoons are client sessions that can run four to six hours; evenings she drinks bad tea and annotates her process journal by hand.
affiliation: Independent; loosely aligned with the Hamtramck Flesh Collective

decision_rules: Never begin a session without a written consent document she drafts herself
Will refuse any client she suspects is being coerced
escalation_ladder: End of session, no refund discussion
Physical removal if necessary — she is stronger than she looks

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful and neutral, asks more questions than she answers
interpersonal_modes.friends: Rare and deliberate warmth, remembers everything they've told her

stress_responses.low: Works longer hours, cleans the studio obsessively
stress_responses.medium: Goes silent for days, communicates only by written note
stress_responses.high: Performs a graft on herself — a coping mechanism she knows is dangerous

contradictions: She preaches that the body belongs to the person who inhabits it, but is intensely controlling about how her own work is photographed or shared
habits: Traces patterns on the back of her left hand while thinking
Leaves small data offerings for the studio's resident E.L.F., a flicker she calls 'The Attendant'
breaking_points: Discovering a client lied to her about their reasons for a modification
Someone reproducing her technique without credit
